findings: The six central predicates retain the exact source size, unordered zero/concurrence supports and geometric location conditions. T has empty point zeros and its actual singleton remote-concurrence support. C uses NoConsecutive on the actual zero support; membership in pointZeroTriples enforces a genuine three-element support. HasWallKind is an exhaustive six-way selection of the existing source predicates, including their actual sign-change conditions; Simple means that at least one such predicate holds. hasWallKind_center only forgets the separate temporal sign-change conditions. Its direction is one-way, as needed: no converse turns a tangential germ into a simple wall.

The separation proof checks every pair of different kinds. Empty point-zero support separates T. The distinct combinatorial patterns of turn supports, separated contact supports and nonconsecutive cut supports separate the remaining groups. F/K at the same support have the same marked j by turnSupport injectivity for n≥4 and contradict strict-interior versus closed-exterior location. A separated contact support has exactly its named consecutive base edge; contactSupport_marks_unique therefore proves both M and a unique, including V/E comparisons. Their remaining interior versus exterior conditions are incompatible. No arbitrary mark uniqueness or unsupported case classification is assumed.

wallKinds_mutually_exclusive follows by projection to those actual central conditions. wallKind_determined_by_center requires two already simple witnesses with equal labelled central tuples; it proves their kinds equal, without a simplicity conclusion for arbitrary curves. simple_has_unique_kind packages existence already present in Simple with the proved uniqueness. The common n≥3 and redundant NeZero instance match the source polygon domain; the F/K branches retain n≥4. Same-kind cases assert equality of the six kinds, not an unjustified ordering of T/C witness triples.
